title: A new boat for the Bar
buys: $40~A crew member's helmet light|$120~A throw line and bag for the boat|$450~A crew drysuit|$2,500~The new boat's searchlight|$12,000~One of its two engines
summary: Margaret Ellwood is twelve years old. Her replacement, ordered for spring 2027, will be faster and better on the Bar at night.
body:
The Bar is where most of our long jobs happen: grounded yachts, people swept out on the ebb, searches after dark. The new boat has better night vision, more room for casualties and a self-righting system rated for breaking water.

The boat costs $285,000 including electronics and engines. Every gift goes to the boat; the appeal's own costs are covered by a local business (fictional).

title: Throw line stations along the town reach
buys: $35~One throw line|$180~One station post and box|$420~A whole station with sign
summary: Ten bank-side boxes with throw lines and instructions, from the weir to the marina. Four are installed.
body: In September a passer-by used the bridge station to pull a teenager out before our boat arrived. Six more stations will cover the rest of the town reach.

title: Thermal camera for night searches
summary: Target met in June. The camera has been used on three night searches since.
body: Thank you to the 402 people who gave. The camera now lives in Rescue 3.

title: Station roof and drying room
buys: $64,000~A new roof and a drying room for kit
body: The crew now have a warm room to dry kit between callouts.
